title: STARMAST
text: Welcome to STARMAST, an accessible, inclusive, and free-to-use bank of online resources in mathematics and statistics made by University of St Andrews staff and students for any student of mathematics or statistics. Please see our about page if you would like to learn more about the project, or our full index to dive in to over 180 pages of written resources!

title: STARMAST
text:
Partners
We are the recommended provider of central University of St Andrews maths and stats support resources, as directed by the Learning and Writing Centre at IELLI at St Andrews.

We would not exist without the Summer Teams Enterprise Programme scheme, and particularly the Vertically Integrated Project scheme, both of which are run at the University of St Andrews.

Finally, we are delighted to have our interactive figures powered by Desmos Studios PBC.

title: Website update: shinylive
text:
Update
Through various updates to R Shinylive, which is the package that powers our interactive statistical figures, the majority of the figures (particularly those involving plots) are now broken on the website.
This has been caused by updates not on our end. I (tdhc) have had a painful few days discovering the problem (in the middle of a national conference!) and trying to fix the error. Ultimately, even after a full un- and re-installation of all of my R packages and machinery, this was all in vain.
However, shinylive did have its issues outside of its finicky set-up; primarily, the long, long loading times were not great in these interactive figures in this day and age. I have therefore begun the process of replacing these with a more robust html + Javascript setup. You can see the differences for yourself in the following images:



Before, using the R Shinylive architecture





After, using the new html + plotly architecture


Currently, I have updated the following three resources:

Factsheet: Normal distribution
Factsheet: Beta distribution
Calculator: \(t\)-testing

and will work on the rest over the summer, along with the fantastic new resources from the 2025/26 S2 VIP crew. Please stay tuned for more :)


Version history

v1.0 initial version written by tdhc 11/06/26.

title: Embedding interactive elements in Quarto
text:
Context

Lecturer (Education Focused) in mathematics
passion for creating good resources / very shallow technical background
currently using Quarto to produce publicly available free-to-use, accessible and inclusive maths and stats support resources
co-create these resources with students as part of a Vertically Integrated Project module at St Andrews

title: Embedding interactive elements in Quarto
text:
Methods (1/2)
wide range of topics necessitate wide range of methods for best results

R package webexercises for ‘quick-check’ questions (true or false, multiple choice…)
Quarto’s synergy with R encourages R Shiny apps, particularly good for statistics

works best with a dedicated R Shiny server (money)
but can use R Shiny Live to run these apps without a server (free, at the cost of longer loading times)

Desmos is best for graphs / recognisable brand for students / accessibility features built-in

can use Desmos API environment for full editability (money)
can embed directly from Desmos without API (free, restricted features)

raw html provides natural flexibility for everything else (calculators, animations…)

title: Embedding interactive elements in Quarto
text:
Methods (2/2)
generative AI provides starting points for use of these tools

R Shiny Assistant (for R Shiny) / Copilot (for html) / ChatGPT (for html/Desmos API environment)
teachable moments for students in using generative AI responsibly
have to ask specifically for accessibility features (standard genAI)

use conditional content tags if using multiple outputs
::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
interactive content
:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
non-interactive content for printable versions
:::

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Problem
need for both accessible and inclusive maths/stats resources

traditional textbooks and learning resources: can be difficult to parse for non-specialists, inaccessible, expensive, intimidating, Western-centric, ‘easy/trivial/obvious’…
diverse backgrounds: every country/region has their own curriculum, language, culture, mathematical stories; every human has their own experience with mathematics and statistics.
increased need for competency in maths/stats

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Perspectives

everyone’s journey in studying mathematics/statistics is different
everyone’s perspective of what is hard and what is easy is different
everyone’s engagement with learning resources is different

I want everyone to be able to access and understand the resources, and I want everyone to feel included in their study of mathematics and statistics.

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Perspectives

communication is audience dependent, and as an educator, my audience could be anybody.
I’m a product of my own perspectives and experiences and these influence the creation of my learning resources.
these perspectives naturally limit the scope, content, format, and dissemination of my resources.

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Solution
ask the audience

On your buzzers please

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Students as co-creators

students provide diverse perspectives needed to create truly inclusive resources.

different cultural backgrounds
different educational backgrounds
different experiences in learning
different mathematical idols

from these experiences, students provide creative and impactful ideas to elevate resources to another level.
creating a free-to-use, high-quality bank of inclusive and technically accessible learning resources in mathematics and statistics, suitable for everyone
in addition, involving students gives learners agency in their resource creation, teaches transferable skills not often found in maths and stats degrees, obtains diverse perspectives on learning…
end product: STARMAST (starmast.org) - St Andrews Resources in Mathematics and Statistics

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
First go: STEP project
Summer Teams Enterprise Programme

online programme over 7 weeks, 4-6 hours work each week
reward is certificate on transcript
teams of 6-7 students, with one paid graduate student acting as ‘coach’
students applied for programme overall, putting projects as first/second choice

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
STARMAST STEP project

ran summer of 2023, aiming for release September 2023
enough interest for two teams of 7 students each producing 12 guides between them, working in smaller teams or individually

topics included rearranging equations, sigma notation, indices and logarithms, trigonometry, vectors

one graduate coach
set up via github containing initial style guide, example guide, questions, answers

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Result
partial success


yes!

all requested resources created
students satisfied with impactful work
framework for expansion in place


 

but

some over-complications

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
What went right?


for me

something to work with!
plenty of questions and answers
basis for expansion
lots of student interest


 

for students

important and impactful project
good opportunity for transferable skills
won something(?) at STEP awards

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
What went wrong?


for me

no control over student selection
disconnected from project
dissatisfied with outputs, took time to put things right


 

for students

little time to communicate with me
long time to see publication (website published and made public May 2024)
teamwork aspect diluted by online programme

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Second go: VIP
Vertically Integrated Project:

multi-year, multi-semester ongoing research project (with some leeway)
students in any year can apply to single projects
awards module credits, and students get a grade for their work
allows students to participate in the same project across multiple years

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Our VIP

small group, weekly meetings, hands-on supervisor involvement
attracting wide range of students

mathematicians, statisticians, economists, cell biologists, computer scientists, art historians…
from first-years to final years

assessment: 20% fortnightly reflective logs, 30% posters and group presentation, 50% final portfolio and reflective report

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Why VIP improved on STEP


for me

full control over student selection
collaboration with students, rather than sponsorship of students
get to teach something out of my comfort zone :)


 

for students

time to communicate with supervisor to float new ideas and understand minor project concerns
module credits (as opposed to a certificate)
chance to be part of a tight-knit team

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
What could be better?

quality of written outputs can be inconsistent (but far far better than STEP project)

increased staff time for quality control

potential duplication of assessment modes for returning students
some student group friction (solution: team building in week 2)

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
What’s gone well?

time for project to breathe and for a team to form
nature of VIP allows for development of big ideas across semesters and years
excellent student buy-in to an impactful and meaningful project
high student satisfaction, both with those who create the resources and those who use the resources
good integration of interdisciplinary skills
outstanding range of outputs

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Students as co-creators (2/2)
not only this, but

students gain agency in their resource creation (what would have helped them in a similar situation?)
development of transferable skills not often found in maths and stats degrees (long form writing, project management, teamwork)
develop empathy for learners / social responsibility / appreciation of other lived experiences, particularly if the focus is on creating accessible and inclusive learning resources.

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Staff as co-creators

project concept and design
advice on time management
facilitator of student learning
guide rather than boss
ultimately, quality control and editing

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
Student involvement

traditionally, the co-creation of resources for learning is generally not a core concern for students studying for a degree; it’s very much an extra-curricular activity

(nowadays, the lines can be blurred!)

in any case, the time, energy, patience, and effort that a student gives to this endeavour should be properly compensated - not only in ‘experience’.
incentivisation can take many different forms!

title: Student-staff co-creation for accessibility and inclusion
text:
An ideal relationship

as equal partners - staff should aim to facilitate rather than directly supervise
